name: Altstadt Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Old Town of Kufstein charms visitors with its iconic fortress, picturesque Römerhofgasse lane, traditional wine taverns, and vibrant Tyrolean inn culture along the Inn River.
preis: Old town freely accessible; Festung Kufstein fortress requires admission ticket
oeffnungszeiten: Old town accessible year-round; fortress grounds open daily
beschreibung:
Überblick

The picturesque Old Town of Kufstein, famously celebrated in song as the 'Pearl of Tirol', nestles beside the emerald waters of the Inn River at the foot of the rugged Kaiser Mountains (Kaisergebirge). For centuries, Kufstein served as the heavily contested gateway between Bavaria and the Austrian lands, endowing the town with a rich defensive history. High above the terracotta rooftops rises the majestic Festung Kufstein, perched upon a dramatic 90-metre limestone crag. In the town center, pastel-hued merchant houses, open squares, and historic gabled facades create an atmospheric urban landscape. Its most beloved gem is the fairytale lane Römerhofgasse: lined with frescoed tavern facades, carved wrought-iron signs, timbered oriel windows, and the historic Auracher Löchl inn, it feels like an open-air museum. Kufstein masterfully unites alpine heritage with modern cultural flair, offering authentic Tyrolean hospitality throughout the seasons.

Route & Anforderungen

Strolling through Kufstein's historical center is completely independent of the weather, barrier-friendly, and delightful for families, heritage enthusiasts, and gourmet travelers. From the central town square (Stadtplatz), leisurely lanes lead into the storied Römerhofgasse and along the scenic riverside promenade beside the Inn. A relaxed exploration takes between one and a half and two and a half hours, depending on time spent browsing independent boutiques and cozy cafés. To visit the fortress, guests may climb the sheltered medieval wooden staircases or glide smoothly upwards aboard the barrier-free Panoramabahn Kaiser Maximilian funicular lift. Flat, comfortable walking shoes are ideal for the paved town lanes, whereas sturdy footwear with rubber soles is advisable for the historic cobblestones and defensive bastions of the fortress.

Besuch & Anreise

Kufstein enjoys superb transport connections, located directly along the Inntal Motorway A12 (exits Kufstein Nord and Kufstein Süd). Convenient multi-storey car parks such as the Kultur Quartier underground garage and Arkadenplatz garage surround the pedestrian core. Rail passengers benefit from Kufstein's central border railway station, served by hourly Eurocity and Railjet express trains from Munich, Innsbruck, and Salzburg. From the station platform, crossing the Inn bridge brings visitors straight into the Stadtplatz and Römerhofgasse within a pleasant five-minute walk.

Tipps

Gather at the town square or fortress terrace precisely at 12:00 noon to hear the daily recital of the Heldenorgel (Heroes' Organ). With 4,948 pipes, it is the largest outdoor organ in the world, sending resonant melodies echoing across the entire valley. Afterward, secure a table in the atmospheric vaults of Römerhofgasse to savor Tyrolean dumplings and regional wines.
